title: Thermochemical recycling of photovoltaic polymer waste: coupled equilibrium and computational fluid dynamics analysis of ethylene-vinyl acetate–backsheet co-gasification
authors: Haider Khan, Sufian Abedrabbo, Isam Janajreh
abstract: End-of-life crystalline silicon photovoltaic (PV) modules are generating a growing stream of polymeric waste dominated by ethylene–vinyl acetate (EVA) encapsulant and fluoropolymer-based backsheet. These materials coexist within the module and are therefore unavoidably co-processed during recycling, yet whose joint thermochemical behavior, and the implications of backsheet-derived fluorine and gasification performance, have not previously been characterised across coupled experimental, thermodynamic, and reactor-scale modelling frameworks. This study presents an experimental characterization and parallel equilibrium-CFD modelling framework to evaluate the co-gasification potential of EVA–backsheet blends recovered from end-of-life PV modules. TGA at multiple heating rates was performed on neat EVA, neat backsheet, and three binary blends (60:40, 40:60, 25:75 by mass) to establish devolatilization behavior and Coats–Redfern kinetic parameters; a Gibbs-energy-minimisation equilibrium model was used to map syngas composition and cold gas efficiency (CGE) across gasification temperatures (750–1923 K) and blend compositions; and the optimal blend was subjected to three-dimensional Euler–Lagrange CFD simulation of an oxygen-blown entrained-flow gasifier incorporating finite-rate homogeneous and heterogeneous chemistry. EVA was found to undergo two-stage devolatilization between 300 and 520 °C with negligible char (<10 wt%), while the PVF/PET backsheet decomposes in a single stage at 440–460 °C, retaining 10–15 wt% char; under co-heating, hydrogen-rich EVA volatiles lower the backsheet onset by 80–100 °C, reducing blend char to ∼ 3 wt%. The 60:40 EVA–backsheet blend achieved the highest equilibrium performance, with a CGE of 69.4% at 1300 °C and syngas mole fractions of H 2 (0.36) and CO (0.40); the corresponding CFD simulation predicted a CGE of 41.4%, approximately 28 percentage points lower, attributable to finite residence time and non-uniform oxygen distribution. These results demonstrate that thermodynamic equilibrium calculations substantially overestimate achievable gasification performance for fluorinated PV polymer waste, and identify blend composition and reactor-scale transport, rather than thermodynamics alone, as the governing levers for designing thermochemical PV-waste recycling systems.
